name: JD Vance
role: Vice President of the United States (2025-present); U.S. senator from Ohio (2023-2025)
summary: Vance is a national-conservative, populist Republican who combines social conservatism, strong opposition to abortion and gender-transition care, and sharply reduced immigration with tariffs, antitrust action and sympathy for striking workers. He champions free-speech arguments against European speech rules, urges Europe to carry its own defense and favors a negotiated end to the Ukraine war, while backing Israel and treating China as the main rival.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: As vice president he said the administration believes tariffs are a necessary tool to protect American jobs and industries, citing auto manufacturing, and he backed Rubio bills with tariffs on Chinese cars as a senator.

free-trade.rationale: Argues the 'logic of globalization' failed and told Rogan the establishment line of 'pro-free trade, everything is good' lets in foreign goods that destroy native industries; supports reshoring through tariffs.

unions-good.rationale: Publicly sided with striking UAW workers in 2023, criticized right-to-work laws and courts union leaders such as Teamsters' O'Brien, though he opposed the PRO Act and the AFL-CIO scores his votes at 0%.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Reported to have criticized right-to-work laws (which bar compulsory union membership or fees); the position is mentioned briefly and the Senate record on it is thin.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Introduced bills to bar undocumented immigrants and DACA recipients from federally funded health benefits and sanctuary cities from housing grants, and said Afghan refugees were being prioritized over citizens; his record concerns unauthorized immigrants more than legal ones.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Said the answer to climate concerns is to produce more American energy 'including fossil fuels'; as vice president he praised steps to cut energy costs and lift environmental regulation and called for reliable power.

limit-growth.rationale: Argues environmental rules pushed manufacturing abroad and that his administration will 'slash regulations' and 'liberate companies from stifling environmental regulations' to build and grow; he treats growth as the goal.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Asked about a climate crisis he answered 'No, I don't think there is, either'; told Rogan the carbon footprint is a distraction from 'real' environmental problems and wanted to repeal Inflation Reduction Act clean-energy credits.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Told Rogan that Germany closing its nuclear plants (with coal) left it dependent on Russian gas, treating the shutdown as a mistake; he has not described a nuclear policy of his own in the sources found.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Rejects the idea that AI should automate away the labor force and says work gives dignity and purpose that welfare or leisure cannot replace.

ban-cartels.rationale: Called for breaking up Google, praised FTC chair Lina Khan's antitrust work and co-sponsored a bill ending tax-free treatment of very large mergers.

corporate-influence.rationale: Told Rogan there is a 'massive corporate lobby for cheap labor' in Congress and that health companies manipulate policy for profit; has said big tech has too much political influence.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Proposed ending the Earned Income Tax Credit marriage penalty and backed a larger child tax credit ($5,000 per child).

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Strong natalist who backed raising the child tax credit to $5,000 per child and has argued that more births and labor-force participation, not cheap imported labor, should sustain the economy and Social Security.

socialized-care.rationale: Said in 2021 that 'universal day care is class war against normal people' because it subsidizes the preferences of the affluent over those of working families who raise children at home.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Said in 2024 he opposed privatizing Social Security and opposed cuts to it and Medicare.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Told Rogan that 'hate speech' is fundamentally subjective and criticized Tim Walz for suggesting it is outside the First Amendment; at Munich he called 'misinformation' and 'disinformation' censorship tools.

limit-guns.rationale: Calls himself 'a big pro-Second Amendment guy'; told Rogan gun regulation cannot solve violence and in 2022 opposed background-check, red-flag and semi-automatic-weapon laws.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Said in 2021 that he wanted to ban pornography and that Americans had chosen the freedom to consume it over public goods such as marriage and family (older statement; no later change found).

internet-shutdowns.rationale: At Munich he condemned EU officials who warned they might shut down social media during civil unrest; this is a criticism of one proposal, not a general statement.

party-controls-media.rationale: Munich and Paris speeches condemn government pressure to censor media and online speech and warn AI must not become a tool of authoritarian censorship.

democracy-best.rationale: Told European leaders that democracy rests on 'the sacred principle that the voice of the people matters' and that they should embrace what voters say 'even when you don't agree'.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Argued at Munich that governments need democratic mandates, cannot win them by censoring opponents, and that dismissing citizens' views destroys democracy.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Describes a 'leadership class' that has failed ordinary workers, officials who ignore voters, and political figures motivated by defense-industry money (told Rogan).

voter-id.rationale: Told Rogan that without voter ID 'you're inviting fraud' and dismissed the argument that it is racist.

suppress-opposition.rationale: At Munich he said 'you cannot win a democratic mandate by censoring your opponents or putting them in jail' and rejected firewalls against populist parties.

traditional-family.rationale: Repeatedly argues for the traditional nuclear family, marriage and children as central to society and has urged policy to favor family formation.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Voted against the Respect for Marriage Act and said marriage is between a man and a woman as a Catholic, while accepting same-sex marriage as the law of the land and saying the issue is not 'alive'.

abortion-legal.rationale: Opposes abortion and supported overturning Roe v. Wade; in 2024 he said states should set abortion law and denied supporting a national ban, and he backs access to mifepristone. Earlier (2022) he said he would like abortion illegal nationally.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Said pursuing 'racial or gender equity' as a value system leads to misery and sponsored a bill to end federal diversity programs.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Speaks of 'biological males' and 'biological females' as distinct categories when arguing against transgender athletes in girls' sports.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Introduced the Passport Sanity Act to block an 'X' passport marker, objected to gender-identity census questions and proposed a federal ban on gender-affirming care for minors.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: After the 2023 Supreme Court ruling he warned top universities that defiance could be unlawful, introduced a College Admissions Accountability bill and a bill to end federal DEI programs.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Introduced a bill making English the official language; the sources do not describe a specific requirement for immigrants.

single-official-language.rationale: Introduced a 2023 bill to make English the official language of the United States.

experts-over-public.rationale: Argues that citizens are not 'interchangeable cogs' and that voters' views should drive policy; attacked the 'public health establishment' and incumbent-driven regulation.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Called mass migration the most urgent challenge facing Western nations, opposes amnesty and in October 2025 said much lower legal immigration would be better for the United States.

open-borders.rationale: Supports a border wall, ended-crossings enforcement and opposes amnesty; calls border security a core priority.

nation-first.rationale: Frames policy as 'America first', says America's interests are sometimes distinct from allies' and Catholic 'ordo amoris' means loving one's own nationals first, while still saying the US wants partners.

force-without-un.rationale: Defended US strikes on Iranian nuclear sites in 2025 and the Venezuela operation; the sources do not record him discussing UN approval itself.

national-mission.rationale: Said he made the mistake of supporting the Iraq War, that he had been lied to by the foreign-policy establishment, and warns against regime-change efforts in Iran.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Said in 2024 the US does not want to leave NATO and wants Europe to take on more of its own defense while the US shifts focus.

close-ties-china.rationale: Calls China the biggest threat to the United States, backs tariffs against it, and told the Paris summit that partnering with authoritarian tech suppliers chains nations to an 'authoritarian master'.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Strong supporter of Israel, which he calls a real ally sharing common values, and backed standalone Israel aid; has not framed this as a statement about a right to statehood.

territorial-expansion.rationale: In March 2025 he said the US 'can't just ignore the president's desires' to acquire Greenland and warned Denmark and rival powers; contested because it is a stated aim of the president he repeated.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Argues that love of country and protecting American workers go together, framing the economy as America first and pro-worker.

notes: Views changed a lot: a 2016 Trump critic ('never-Trump guy') he became an ally from 2021, and the most recent clear position is used throughout. Positions on abortion shifted from wanting a national ban (2022) to leaving it to the states (2024). Only the Munich, Paris and American Dynamism speeches and the Rogan interview were available as full text; the 2024 RNC speech, vice-presidential debate, NatCon 2021 speech and Senate bill texts could not be retrieved in full, so many Senate-record answers rest on the Wikipedia article and Roll Call reporting (medium confidence unless a quote is given). Living person: nothing inferred from party or label; contested items such as the 'replacement' remarks were left null.
